what_happened: The parallel-jobs job failed at admission twice. The operator traced the cause: admission parses a changed athena.toml using the schema of the running binary, so a job cannot add a new config section. The operator then ordered a fix ahead of retrying the parallel-jobs work. They did this by hand, outside Athena's plan.
cause: Admission validates a job's proposed athena.toml against the schema compiled into the running binary. A job that adds a config section together with the code that accepts it is therefore always refused. The schema change and the config change cannot ship in one job. Nothing detects this in advance, and Athena retried instead of diagnosing it. The operator had to find the root cause and sequence a separate fix first.
prevention: Change admission so it can accept a config change that comes with the schema change in the same job. For example, validate the changed athena.toml against the schema from the job's own proposed code, or treat config sections the binary does not know as pending until the schema lands. Also add a pre-admission check that flags a config edit using fields the running schema rejects. When it fires, it should report that the schema change must go first and split the work into schema then config. It should not fail repeatedly.
proposed_request: Make job admission able to accept a job that adds a new athena.toml section together with the code that makes the schema accept it. Outcome: a job that changes both the config schema and athena.toml is admitted and runs. Admission must not refuse it because the running binary does not yet know the section. A config edit that really is invalid under the job's own resulting schema must still be refused with a clear message. Add a test that submits a job adding a new config section with its schema support and checks it is admitted. Add a second test that a truly invalid config is still refused. After that, retry the parallel-jobs request.
